definitions.explanation: Describes a lifestyle, appearance, or object that is simple and unpretentious, without luxury or extravagance. Often carries positive connotations of modesty and good values.

examples.japanese: {質素|しっそ}な{食事|しょくじ}だが、{栄養|えいよう}は{十分|じゅうぶん}だ。
examples.english: The meal is simple but nutritious enough.

examples.japanese: {質素|しっそ}{倹約|けんやく}を{旨|むね}として{生|い}きてきた{祖父母|そふぼ}を{尊敬|そんけい}している。
examples.english: I respect my grandparents who have lived by the principle of simple frugality.

notes:
ADJECTIVE TYPE: Na-adjective. Uses な before nouns: {質素|しっそ}な{生活|せいかつ}.

ADVERBIAL FORM: {質素|しっそ}に (simply, frugally)

NUANCE: {質素|しっそ} typically has positive connotations - it suggests admirable simplicity and lack of pretension rather than poverty. It's often associated with traditional Japanese values of modesty.

FOUR-CHARACTER COMPOUND: {質素|しっそ}{倹約|けんやく} (simple and frugal) is a common phrase describing a modest, thrifty lifestyle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {質素|しっそ}な{暮|く}らし/{生活|せいかつ} (simple life)
- {質素|しっそ}な{食事|しょくじ} (simple meal)
- {質素|しっそ}{倹約|けんやく} (simple frugality)
- {質素|しっそ}に{暮|く}らす (to live simply)

RELATED WORDS:
- {簡素|かんそ} (simple, plain - similar)
- {地味|じみ} (plain, subdued)
- {倹約|けんやく} (thrift, economy)
- {華麗|かれい} (splendid, gorgeous - opposite)
- {豪華|ごうか} (luxurious - opposite)
